mission: Evaluate a shared LumenShell architecture that can support a person during ground tasks or operate unoccupied as an autonomous robotic platform, with a physically detachable experimental propulsion module.
current_program_boundary: Ground and unoccupied test research only. Human flight is outside the authorized prototype program until independent aerospace, medical, safety, and regulatory authorities approve a later program.

mode_definitions.WEARABLE_GROUND: Verified occupant is primary authority; bounded assist only; propulsion remains deenergized.
mode_definitions.AUTONOMOUS_GROUND: No occupant; autonomous controller may command bounded ground motion inside a controlled exclusion zone.
mode_definitions.PROPULSION_TEST_STAND: Detached propulsion module is physically locked to an instrumented stand with no occupant.
mode_definitions.AUTONOMOUS_TETHERED_TEST: No occupant; integrated system is physically tethered and operated under independent test authorization.
mode_definitions.FAULT_LOCKOUT: Energy and motion are removed; only a deliberate service reset can return the system to SAFE_GROUND.

architectural_separation: independent safety controller and hardwired energy isolation
separate electric-vehicle honeycomb battery research lane

requirements.shall: The system shall implement mutually exclusive wearable, autonomous, propulsion-test, safe-ground, powered-off, and fault-lockout states.
The propulsion module shall be mechanically, electrically, and logically detachable from the ground exosuit.
An independent safety controller shall retain authority to remove actuator and propulsion energy regardless of mission-controller state.
Autonomous and propulsion-test states shall be rejected whenever any independent occupancy sensor reports a person in the suit.
Every active-mode transition shall begin from SAFE_GROUND with actuators and propulsion deenergized.
Emergency stop, watchdog loss, sensor-health loss, or isolation fault shall make FAULT_LOCKOUT reachable without software permission from a mission controller.
Wearable operation shall require verified harness closure, joint alignment, quick release, egress, and ground support.
No current software state shall authorize occupied flight.
Propulsion testing shall require a locked stand or independent physical tether, a clear exclusion zone, and written independent safety authorization.
Stored-energy domains shall provide independent isolation, current limiting, thermal monitoring, containment intent, and service disconnects.
Wearable intent assistance and autonomous behavior shall use separate bounded controllers and shall not share unrestricted command authority.
All safety-relevant commands, interlock observations, clock sources, configuration versions, and state transitions shall be time-stamped and hash-receipted.
Lift and control authority shall be supported only by measured thrust, mass, power, thermal, and failure-envelope evidence from instrumented tests.
Propulsion hazards shall be assessed for ingestion, hot surfaces, debris, rotor containment, asymmetric thrust, loss of power, fire, noise, and uncontrolled motion.

Sound and frequency functions shall be limited to measurable sensing, ranging, communication, modal identification, vibration control, noise control, and health monitoring unless a new claim passes independent testing.
The program shall not claim that acoustic or cymatic effects provide human-scale primary lift without independent reproducible evidence.
Wave-channel structures shall be compared against flat-panel, straight-rib, and conventional constrained-layer damping baselines under identical blinded protocols.
Human-factors evaluation shall cover fit range, pressure, pinch and crush zones, joint alignment, center-of-mass shift, balance, fatigue, thermal exposure, noise, and emergency egress.
Remote and autonomous functions shall fail closed under authentication loss, command replay, stale telemetry, clock drift, network loss, or software integrity failure.
The program shall obtain written regulatory-pathway guidance before any free-flight activity or public operation.

authority_gates.name: Source and claim boundary
authority_gates.pass_evidence: Dated concept lineage, public/private boundary, prior-art review plan, and claim-risk register approved.

authority_gates.name: Requirements and hazards
authority_gates.pass_evidence: Independent review of requirements, hazard analysis, FMEA, system safety assessment, and verification matrix.

authority_gates.name: Passive fit and egress
authority_gates.pass_evidence: Unpowered fit rig demonstrates joint alignment, load paths, quick release, egress, and no unacceptable pinch or pressure hazards.

authority_gates.name: Frequency and structure evidence
authority_gates.pass_evidence: Preregistered coupon tests report damping, transmissibility, fatigue, thermal, mass, and uncertainty results against named baselines.

authority_gates.name: Ground actuation and autonomy
authority_gates.pass_evidence: Tethered joint rigs and unoccupied ground platform pass interlock, balance, stop-distance, watchdog, and fault-injection tests.

authority_gates.name: Detached propulsion stand
authority_gates.pass_evidence: Qualified facility independently witnesses contained static tests and reports thrust, power, thermal, noise, vibration, containment, and failure data.

authority_gates.name: Unoccupied integrated tether
authority_gates.pass_evidence: No-occupant integrated system passes tethered tests, asymmetric-fault tests, deterministic replay, and independent test-readiness review.

authority_gates.name: Authority hold point
authority_gates.pass_evidence: Independent aerospace, medical, safety, and regulatory authorities approve the next test basis in writing. Passing this gate is not itself certification or permission for unrestricted operation.

acoustic_frequency_test_matrix.hypothesis: Wave-channel panels improve structural damping without unacceptable mass or thermal penalties.
Active vibration control reduces selected structural modes under bounded operating conditions.
Acoustic and vibration telemetry improves propulsion health-event detection.
